sections.title: Media you choose
sections.body: Lumen Studio edits photos, videos and audio you select through Android's picker or Files. It does not request access to your entire photo or video library. Android may offer files from a cloud provider; retrieving those files is handled by Android or that provider. Processing within Lumen Studio happens on your device.

sections.title: Local editing data
sections.body: Drafts store file references, filenames, clip timing and your edits, including authored text. Imported or extracted sounds, generated stickers and freeze frames are stored privately by the app. If a provider cannot retain file access, the app may keep a private copy so a draft can be reopened. Source files must remain accessible unless privately copied.

sections.title: Collection and sharing
sections.body: This connected edition offers optional usage analytics and text-only support through the developer-operated API. It does not upload photos, videos, audio, project files, filenames or authored project text. Exported files are saved to the destination you choose. The external service you choose for sharing handles the exported file under its own terms. This edition includes third-party advertising SDKs described below.

sections.title: Optional usage analytics
sections.body: Share usage analytics is off by default. If you enable it, the app sends a random installation ID, brand/model, Android API level, screen density, configured locale/region, app version and counters for app opens, completed video exports, image-edit starts selected feature IDs and advertising-impression placement IDs to the administrator. Locale region is not verified physical location. This administrator analytics channel does not use advertising IDs, IMEI, serial numbers, GPS location or a hardware fingerprint. Advertising providers have separate practices described below. The installation ID can change after reinstalling or clearing app data. We use the records to understand use and compatibility, not to identify a person. You may stop sharing in Settings without losing editing functionality.

sections.title: Remote ad settings
sections.body: When the connected app is in the foreground, it periodically fetches public versioned ad-placement settings without an installation identifier. The app applies enabled routes and IDs only in the advertising edition and only after the applicable privacy checks. The server receives the network connection needed for this request. Advertising SDKs can process data separately as described below. Dashboard changes normally reach a connected foreground app within about one minute; stale or failed configuration checks stop new ad requests.

sections.title: Retention and deletion
sections.body: Local drafts remain until you delete them or clear Android app storage. Delete drafts in Projects and sounds in the sound library. Original media and exports outside private app storage remain under your control. On the server, detailed usage events are retained for up to 90 days, daily usage totals for up to 365 days, support conversations for up to 180 days after their last update, and inactive installation records for up to 365 days after their last authenticated activity. Turning off Share usage analytics saves your choice immediately and requests removal of usage history and device profile; if offline, the request is retried when the app next opens with a connection. Support conversations remain. Settings > Delete online data removes this installation record, usage history and support conversations when the request succeeds. Clearing Android app storage alone does not delete server records and may remove the credential needed to request deletion; contact the administrator for assistance. New installations cannot automatically recover earlier conversations.

sections.title: Permissions and reminders
sections.body: Notifications are optional and off by default. When enabled, generic editing reminders are scheduled approximately every three hours, including overnight, subject to Android delivery rules. You can disable them in Settings or Android notification settings. Media is accessed only after you choose it. The app does not request camera, microphone, location, contacts or device-wide storage permissions.

sections.title: Contacting support
sections.body: When you press Send in Contact Us, the app sends your reason, description and a random installation ID to the administrator through the configured API. Replies are delivered to Support inbox when you open it. Support is available without enabling usage analytics. No attachments or SMS permission are used. Avoid sending passwords or sensitive information in messages. The configured hosting/database provider processes the messages to operate support. The administrator can read and respond to these conversations.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Media and drafts remain in Android app-private or user-selected storage; app backup is disabled. Public API connections require HTTPS. A random per-installation credential protects access to your support conversations. Only local debug builds allow HTTP to approved loopback/emulator addresses. The server holds credential hashes and administrator password hashes. The hosting provider necessarily receives network connection information such as the source IP; the local implementation uses IP addresses transiently for rate limiting and does not store them in its database. Production hosting and logging practices must be documented before publication.

sections.title: Accounts, purchases and audiences
sections.body: This edition does not create user accounts or sell subscriptions or in-app purchases. There is no account to delete. The developer must declare the intended audience and age rating accurately before release; this test policy does not claim a verified child-directed service.

sections.title: Policy changes
sections.body: The effective date above identifies this version. If data handling changes, including adding cloud processing, advertising or other SDKs, the policy and store declarations must be updated before that edition is published.

sections.title: Advertising and mediation
sections.body: Google AdMob mediates advertising from Google and configured partners: Meta Audience Network, ironSource Ads (Unity), Unity Ads and AppLovin. Participating SDKs may process advertising identifiers when available, IP address, approximate location inferred from IP, device and app information, diagnostics, ad interactions and fraud-prevention signals. These providers process data to deliver ads, measure performance, prevent fraud and comply with legal obligations under their own privacy notices. Photos, videos, project files, filenames and authored text are not sent to the admin server or intentionally supplied in ad requests. Non-personalized advertising can still require these technical data and applicable consent.

sections.title: Advertising choices and optional rewards
sections.body: Where required, a Google User Messaging Platform form collects privacy choices before ad requests. Required advertising privacy options can be reopened from Settings. Google ad requests are restricted to non-personalized ads; partner data practices and consent settings still apply. A voluntary rewarded ad pauses further ad requests for 30 minutes in the current app session only after the network reports the reward. Dismissing or declining an ad leaves normal editing and exporting available. Ad availability is not guaranteed. Existing ads can remain visible while a request or privacy update is being processed.

sections.title: Configuration delivery diagnostics
sections.body: The app retrieves public versioned advertising settings from the administrator API. For users who enable optional usage analytics, it additionally reports the received configuration version, whether the build includes advertising, app version and receipt time, associated with the random installation ID. These diagnostics confirm settings delivery, not that an ad was shown. Opting out requests deletion of these receipts and usage history. No advertising configuration receipt is sent for users who have not opted into usage analytics.

sections.title: Advertising provider privacy notices
sections.body: Google: https://policies.google.com/privacy ; Meta: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/ ; Unity and ironSource: https://unity.com/legal/privacy-policy ; AppLovin: https://www.applovin.com/privacy/ . Contact the developer for questions or requests concerning data held by this application. Providers may offer their own access, deletion or opt-out procedures.
